nodes.venue: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
nodes.abstract: This article aimed to analyze the role of Primary Health Care in controlling endemic diseases in the Amazon region, identifying structural and organizational challenges that influence the response capacity of health services. It is an integrative review of scientific articles published between 2021 and 2024 in the SciELO, PubMed, and VHL (BVS) databases, combining the descriptors "Primary Health Care," "Endemic Diseases," "Amazon," "Leprosy," and "Chagas Disease." The results show that leprosy and Chagas disease remain significant public health issues in the region, exacerbated by social vulnerabilities, limitations in health service infrastructure, and difficulties in the early detection of cases. Primary Health Care plays a strategic role in health surveillance but faces limitations related to a shortage of professionals, staff turnover, and geographical barriers. The study concludes that strengthening Primary Health Care, through the expansion of health surveillance strategies and the professional development of health workers, is essential for addressing endemic diseases in the Amazon.

nodes.name: Revista Ibero-Americana de Humanidades, Ciências e Educação
Vision–language foundation models for multimodal medical image understanding and report generation: a narrative review with quantitative synthesis
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Medicine
nodes.abstract: Vision-language foundation models (VLFMs) for medical image understanding have advanced rapidly, yet evidence supporting clinical deployment remains fragmented. This narrative review synthesizes architectures, training paradigms, benchmarks, public datasets, and translation barriers. Drawing on more than 50 original studies published between 2020 and 2025, we provide a structured descriptive comparison rather than a statistical meta-analysis. In a focused audit of 13 representative studies, BLEU/ROUGE was reported by 31% (4/13), RadGraph F1 by 0% (0/13), CheXpert- or CheXbert-derived label evaluation by 46% (6/13), BERTScore by 8% (1/13), human expert evaluation by 31% (4/13), and inference latency or throughput by 0% (0/13). Because datasets, splits, candidate pools, and metrics differ, cross-task results are presented as exploratory benchmark indicators and not as a clinical-readiness scale. The synthesis identifies persistent concerns involving hallucination, limited interpretability, distribution shift, and narrow demographic and geographic coverage. We propose a minimum clinical validation and reporting standard aligned with the distinct purposes of FDA/Health Canada/MHRA and IMDRF Good Machine Learning Practice, the EU AI Act, TRIPOD+AI, and CLAIM, and identify eleven priority research directions. Medical VLFMs are promising, but progress should be judged by source-traceable, clinically grounded, and externally validated evidence.

nodes.name: Satellite evidence of fertilizer-driven, temperature-dependent ammonia emissions
nodes.abstract: Abstract Agricultural ammonia (NH3) emissions are strongly influenced by environmental conditions and management practices, yet how fertilizer type shapes the temperature response of volatilization at large scales remains poorly understood. Here we show, using a 16-year record of daily NH3 total columns from the Infrared Atmospheric Sounding Interferometer, that the dependence of atmospheric NH3 on skin temperature diverges into two fundamentally different responses. In regions less reliant on urea, NH3 columns increase monotonically with skin temperature, matching the classical process-based representation of NH3 volatilization. In urea-dominated regions, by contrast, NH3 columns rise quasi-exponentially to a characteristic breakpoint between 310 and 318 K, above which they decline sharply. This discontinuity, revealed here for the first time using a large observational dataset, is consistent across urea-dominated regions. We hypothesize that this discontinuity reflects a temperature-limited NHx supply in urea-dominated systems, potentially mediated by urease-catalyzed hydrolysis and modulated by local environmental conditions. These findings identify fertilizer type, soil characteristics, and climate variability as key drivers of NH3 volatilization, and suggest that their combined effects must be represented in models to improve emission predictions and anticipate climate impacts on air quality and nitrogen deposition.

nodes.name: SC-MAPS: Image-based deep learning for bacterial identification and antibiotic-susceptibility testing
nodes.abstract: Rapid bacterial identification could help guide antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST), but image-based classification must generalise across bacterial strains. We developed SC-MAPS, a multichannel microscopy dataset comprising 916,435 single cells from 13 bacterial species, with independent strains reserved for evaluation. Combining phase-contrast and fluorescence information using deep learning achieved 65.4% single-cell species-classification accuracy on held-out strains. To assess whether imperfect species predictions retained useful information for downstream testing, we defined eight antimicrobial-resistance-informed AST-routing groups. Pooling species probabilities increased routing accuracy to 77.1%, rising to 91.1% when predictions from five cells were combined and 96.2% with 20 cells. Synthetic mixtures revealed limitations in minority-species recovery, while exploratory analysis of unseen organisms demonstrated the potential for out-of-distribution detection. SC-MAPS provides a framework for investigating transferable bacterial phenotypes and developing image-based identification and AST-routing strategies.

nodes.name: Relationship between apathy, glymphatic dysfunction, and white matter integrity in Parkinson’s disease: a multimodal MRI study
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Aging Neuroscience
nodes.abstract: Background Apathy is a disabling non-motor symptom of Parkinson’s disease (PD), but its neuroimaging correlates remain unclear. Glymphatic-related MRI metrics abnormalities and white matter microstructural damage have each been implicated in PD, yet their relationship with apathy is incompletely understood. Objective To investigate the relationships among glymphatic-related MRI metrics, white matter abnormalities, and apathy in PD, while accounting for affective, cognitive, motor, and treatment-related factors. Methods We prospectively enrolled 41 patients with PD [19 with apathy (APD), 22 without apathy (nAPD)] and 38 healthy controls (HC). Multimodal MRI quantified choroid plexus volume (CPV), perivascular space measures, DTI-ALPS, gBOLD-CSF coupling, free water (FW), free-water-corrected diffusion indices, and NODDI metrics. Tract-based spatial statistics, sparse principal component analysis, partial correlation, sensitivity analyses, and exploratory mediation analyses were performed. Results Compared with HC, PD patients showed widespread white matter abnormalities, including increased FW, fwAD, fwMD, fwRD, and ODI and decreased fwFA and NDI. APD patients showed higher FW than nAPD patients in clusters involving the corpus callosum, left superior longitudinal fasciculus, uncinate fasciculus, inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus, and other widespread tracts. Within PD, these FW abnormalities were associated with apathy severity; several associations persisted after adjustment for UPDRS-III and levodopa equivalent daily dose but were attenuated after adjustment for affective or cognitive symptoms. CPV measures were also associated with apathy-related FW abnormalities, with selected associations remaining after adjustment for MoCA or motor/medication measures. Direct associations between individual glymphatic-related MRI metrics and apathy severity were less consistent. Exploratory mediation effects were observed mainly in the combined PD + HC cohort and were not robust within PD or apathy subgroups after multiple-comparison correction. Conclusion Apathy in PD was most consistently associated with increased extracellular FW within distributed white matter networks, superimposed on widespread PD-related microstructural damage. Glymphatic-related MRI metrics abnormalities, particularly CPV, were coupled with apathy-related FW but showed weaker direct relationships with apathy severity. These findings support an associative glymphatic–white matter framework for PD apathy, while suggesting partial overlap with broader affective and cognitive dysfunction rather than an apathy-specific causal cascade.

nodes.name: Process effect prediction method based on visual generative models
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract This study aims to develop a conditional visual generation model that maps process-structure relationships, generating scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of metallographic microstructures under specified conditions based on input process parameters for process improvement reference. The Omni-loss is used to optimize the conditional discriminator/generator. A MAE-CGAN model was proposed to demonstrate the fidelity of generated microstructures and their correlation with applied processing methods. The model integrating visual transformer and Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGAN) offers several advantages: the CGAN framework theoretically supports modeling any material system; trained generators can produce specific microstructure images under designated process conditions. And the prediction datasets are evaluated using quantitative indicators proposed in previous work. The results showed that the pre-trained Masked Auto-Encoder (MAE) model demonstrated robust critical structural feature extraction capabilities with the relatively small image dataset. The quantitative analysis of existing samples yielded results consistent with the expert evaluations, and the generated samples hold great potential for guiding future experimental settings.

nodes.name: Operational monitoring of urban coastal pollution: integrating satellite remote sensing and machine learning to manage turbid and suspected sewage plumes
nodes.venue: Anthropocene Coasts
nodes.abstract: Abstract Effective management of urban coastal pollution is often hindered by an inability to track the spatial and seasonal dynamics of wastewater plumes from creeks and canals. This study addresses this management gap by developing and validating a satellite-based operational monitoring framework for one of the polluted creeks in the Chennai metropolitan city, and adjacent coastal waters of the Bay of Bengal, India. The present study assessed water quality and plume dynamics using monthly one cloud free data from January 2023 to December 2025. Satellite-derived Chlorophyll-a and Total Suspended Matter were processed using the Case 2 Regional Coast Colour processor, and turbidity was estimated using a semi-empirical algorithm. Retrieved products were validated against synchronous in-situ measurements from two different field campaigns, demonstrating a strong positive correlation. Time-series analysis revealed low turbidity or no plume events during the dry season and extensive, highly turbid plumes during the Northeast Monsoon season (October to December) with plume extension observed up to 5 km offshore. A Random Forest classifier was trained using unsupervised K-means++ clustering of > 80,000 remote sensing reflectance spectra from a representative high-discharge (15 th November 2024) event produced 14 spectrally distinct optical water types, ranging from clear marine waters to anomalously polluted types characterized by elevated red and near-infrared reflectance. This hybrid approach provides a robust framework for the spatial detection and monitoring of coastal discharges. This framework enables early warning of pollution events, supports compliance tracking with environmental regulations, and allows targeted interventions to reduce ecological impacts. This approach demonstrates how readily available satellite data and machine learning can be operationalized to improve coastal water quality management in rapidly urbanizing regions facing similar challenges.

nodes.name: Observation operator and detection limits for MODIS and VIIRS Fire Radiative Power products
nodes.venue: Geoscientific Model Development
nodes.abstract: We analyze the MODIS and VIIRS active-fire Fire Radiative Power (FRP) products, suggest an approximation for the FRP detection limit as a linear function of a pixel area, and develop analytical observation operators for both pixel-level and gridded FRP products. We have shown that the collection-6.1 of MODIS has the FRP detection limit at 3.7 MW in case of a nadir retrieval at a clear-sky night. For a daytime sideview, it reaches as high as 40 MW. For VIIRS, the smallest fire reliably detected at night is 0.5 MW. Application of the developed operators for the cross-mapping the MODIS and VIIRS datasets at the pixel/granule level confirmed their consistency. Applying the grid-level operators alongside satellite overpass and weather data, we generated global maps of fire detection probabilities, revealing regional variations. As a global average, probability of detection of powerful fires is 78 % for MODIS (88 % for VIIRS). Variations between regions are large: in some equatorial areas this probability is less than 30 % for MODIS (40 % for VIIRS).

nodes.name: Multimodal In Vivo Imaging of Cutaneous Angiogenesis: A Structured Narrative Review of Dermoscopy, Dynamic OCT, and Line-Field Confocal OCT
nodes.venue: Diagnostics
nodes.abstract: Aims: This structured narrative review aimed to synthesize and critically appraise the available human evidence on in vivo assessment of cutaneous angiogenesis using dermoscopy, dynamic optical coherence tomography (D-OCT), and line-field confocal optical coherence tomography (LC-OCT), and to determine whether disease-specific microvascular phenotypes can be defined across selected neoplastic and inflammatory dermatoses. Type of review. Structured narrative review (SNAR), using SANRA as a narrative-review quality framework. The work was not designed as a systematic review of diagnostic accuracy and was not prospectively registered. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to November 2025 using combinations of terms for angiogenesis, cutaneous vasculature, dermoscopy, OCT, D-OCT, LC-OCT, OCT angiography, melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, actinic keratosis, squamous neoplasia, Bowen disease, psoriasis, and Kaposi sarcoma. The clinical synthesis focused on original human studies; technical reviews and preclinical sources were used for background only. Findings: Findings were synthesized qualitatively because imaging protocols and vascular terminology were too heterogeneous for meta-analysis. Salient findings. Angiogenic architecture is disease-patterned rather than uniform. D-OCT studies associate melanoma vascular morphology with Breslow thickness, without establishing a validated optical staging test. Basal cell carcinoma shows hierarchically organized arborizing stromal vessels. Bowen disease shows glomerular, horizontally oriented units, whereas actinic keratosis shows milder, grade-dependent remodeling; multimodal imaging remains limited in separating hypertrophic actinic keratosis from early squamous cell carcinoma. Psoriasis shows elongated, regularly distributed dilated papillary loops, distinct from the less organized pattern of eczematous dermatitis. Kaposi sarcoma imaging evidence remains preliminary and does not establish stage-specific vascular criteria. Plexus depth is measurable and differs among some diseases and adjacent skin, but it is not a standalone marker of invasiveness. LC-OCT adds near-histologic three-dimensional morphology; D-OCT adds perfusion and depth; dermoscopy remains the accessible surface map. Conclusions: Multimodal in vivo imaging can link surface vascular clues to structural and functional substrates of cutaneous angiogenesis and can improve interpretive separation of disease-specific patterns from non-specific inflammatory remodeling. Most proposed quantitative biomarkers, including plexus depth, remain preliminary and require standardized descriptors and prospective multicenter validation, including studies with inflamed mimics, before routine clinical use.

nodes.name: Multi-source satellite remote sensing of harmful algal blooms in the East China Sea: cross-sensor comparison of GOCI, Sentinel-2 and Sentinel-3
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Marine Science
nodes.abstract: Introduction Harmful algal blooms (HABs) represent recurring coastal ecological hazards that threaten aquaculture, marine ecosystems and near‑shore environmental safety. Satellite remote sensing provides essential observational capacity for HAB monitoring; nevertheless, systematic quantitative inter‑comparisons between geostationary GOCI‑II and polar‑orbiting Sentinel‑2 MSI / Sentinel‑3 OLCI for identical bloom events remain limited. This study addresses the complementary strengths and limitations of these three ocean‑colour sensors for East China Sea HAB observation. Methods We selected two well‑documented HAB episodes occurring in the East China Sea during 2021 (30 April and 22 September). GOCI‑II, Sentinel‑2 MSI and Sentinel‑3 OLCI datasets were processed using sensor‑matched atmospheric correction schemes (standard GOCI‑II ocean‑colour processing, ACOLITE‑DSF for Sentinel‑2, C2RCC for Sentinel‑3 OLCI). Six spectral indices including NDCI, RBD, NRTI, RAB, PDI and DI were applied for bloom detection. Spatial‑degradation experiments at 20 m, 300 m and 500 m were implemented to separate geometric scale‑related effects on bloom area and boundary representation. Near‑simultaneous overpass comparisons and hourly GOCI‑II time‑series tracking were performed to quantify inter‑sensor discrepancies and intra‑day bloom dynamics. Results Under ~10‑minute near‑coincident overpass on 30 April 2021, GOCI‑II mapped a bloom area of 901.52 km² versus 571.52 km² from Sentinel‑2B; the difference originated jointly from spatial resolution, spectral configuration, atmospheric correction and detection thresholds, while bloom advection exerted minor influence. On 22 September 2021, hourly GOCI‑II observations captured a complete intra‑day bloom cycle: bloom optical‑anomaly area varied from 37.30 km² up to a peak of 760.20 km² and declined to 107.67 km², accompanied by a 45.74 km centroid displacement, a dynamic that single polar‑orbiting snapshots only partially captured. Spatial degradation analysis demonstrated that boundary‑length loss exceeded 76 – 85 % at coarser resolutions, whereas total‑area deviations ranged from −14.8 % to +11.0 %, highlighting Sentinel‑2’s unique value for fine‑scale near‑shore boundary delineation. Even after resolution normalisation, substantial spatial mismatch persisted among sensor bloom products (IoU as low as 0.014). Discussion Individual sensors exhibit distinct trade‑offs: GOCI‑II delivers high‑frequency temporal screening, Sentinel‑2 provides fine‑scale spatial detail, and Sentinel‑3 OLCI supplies rich spectral information for regional contextual analysis. Accordingly, we propose a conditional three‑stage multi‑source synergistic workflow: GOCI‑II for rapid hourly screening and drift tracking, Sentinel‑2 MSI for priority‑zone fine‑scale inspection, and Sentinel‑3 OLCI for regional spectral validation and cross‑sensor consistency checking. Discrepancies across sensors stem from combined effects of spectral band configuration, atmospheric correction, index thresholds and sampling timing. Limitations include only two analysed bloom events and absence of dense pixel‑level in‑situ ground truth. Further multi‑event validation with harmonised atmospheric correction is required to generalise this conditional monitoring template for operational HAB early‑warning in optically‑complex East Asian coastal waters.

nodes.name: IoT-enabled multimodal large language model-based framework for compositional food recognition, nutrient profiling, NOVA classification, and cancer risk mitigation
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Nutrition
nodes.abstract: Background Automated dietary assessment increasingly struggles to evaluate industrial food processing levels, revealing a systemic gap between the visual presentation of meals and their underlying ultra-processed food composition. Although existing dietary monitoring tools can effectively track caloric and macronutrient intake, they lack the qualitative processing assessments required to identify hidden additives and map dietary risk triage quadrants. Methods This study introduces a modular, IoT-enabled multimodal dietary decision-support framework that decouples visual food recognition, standardized database retrieval, and qualitative language reasoning for automated NOVA processing classification and 2D decision matrix mapping. Operating on isolated single-dish meal instances, the system employs a four-phase cascaded pipeline that integrates vision-language models, database retrieval, and large language models (LLMs) with strict JSON schema enforcement. The platform was evaluated using the Nutrition-NOVA validation benchmark, a harmonized multimodal dataset constructed through dense vector-space semantic linkage between quantitative profiles from the Center for Food Safety database and qualitative NOVA tiers from Open Food Facts. This benchmark addresses a 75.0% metadata sparsity deficit identified in legacy repositories. Results In experimental evaluations on the Nutrition-NOVA benchmark, the baseline Qwen-VL-Max architecture achieved an adjacent accuracy of 77.7%. Furthermore, enforcing schema modularity enabled complete plug-and-play backend replaceability between commercial cloud application programming interfaces (APIs) and private, on-premises open-weight models without requiring architectural retraining. Discussion The proposed framework establishes an efficient, safety-first screening tool for digital healthcare decision support. By isolating qualitative LLM reasoning from visual perceptual noise and database metadata sparsity, the system successfully bridges the gap between intuitive meal perception and point-of-care dietary risk triage, offering a non-invasive and scalable solution for automated dietary auditing and longitudinal population health monitoring.

nodes.name: Intelligent Detection Algorithm for Garment Pattern Defects Based on Computer Vision and Deep Learning
nodes.venue: International Journal of e-Collaboration
nodes.abstract: This work suggests an Intelligent Detection Algorithm for Garment Pattern Defects Based on Computer Vision and Deep Learning (IDAGPD-DL), a deep learning-based intelligent system that will be used to detect and classify the defects in garment pattern products by incorporating computer vision preprocessing, optimized feature extraction, and an optimized neural network design. The method can capture spatial and structural differences in stitching and fabric designs, enabling efficient defect localization and correct classification. An experimental analysis of an open-source garment stitching defect dataset shows that IDAGPD-DL achieves 96.3% detection accuracy, 95.1% precision, 94.6% recall, and 94.8% F1-score, which is better than current baseline methods by about 7-10 points across all performance metrics. These findings demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly reduce misclassification rates and improve detection reliability, making it well-suited for real-time quality control in a smart garment production system.

nodes.name: How Much Does the Classifier Matter? A Cluster-Aware Comparison of Six Machine Learning Algorithms for Land Use Land Cover Mapping of Taipei, Taiwan, Using Google Earth Engine and Python
nodes.venue: ICCK Journal of Image Analysis and Processing
nodes.abstract: Comparative studies of machine learning classifiers for Land Use Land Cover (LULC) mapping often recommend one algorithm, yet their validation pixels are usually drawn from a few hand-digitised polygons and are far from independent. This study tested whether such differences survive that dependence. Six classifiers, namely Classification and Regression Tree (CART), Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), a multilayer perceptron and a support vector machine (SVM) with a radial basis function kernel, were applied to four top-of-atmosphere bands of a 2020 annual Sentinel-2 median composite of Taipei City, Taiwan, at 10~m. All 110 reference polygons were kept whole in both the hold-out split and the tuning folds. Pairwise differences were tested with the standard and the cluster-corrected McNemar test, and accuracies and class areas were estimated with the Olofsson stratified estimator on the effective sample size. Hold-out overall accuracy ranged only from 0.927 (CART) to 0.956 (SVM). The 1,829 validation pixels came from 30 polygons and, with a design effect of 71-76, were equivalent to only 24-26 independent observations. Eight of the fifteen pairwise differences were significant under the standard test, but none remained significant after the cluster correction. Mapped areas nevertheless differed markedly between models, from 71.7 to 102.1~km$^2$ for built-up land and from 10.9 to 32.2~km$^2$ for swamp; for built-up land, the between-model spread was as large as the sampling uncertainty of a single map. The six classifiers are therefore statistically indistinguishable in accuracy, and the choice among them should rest on computational cost, which differed by a factor of about 330 at inference, and on the stability of the areas they produce.

nodes.name: ICCK Journal of Image Analysis and Processing
FineKarstAGB: a 30 m resolution aboveground biomass dataset for Southwest China derived by upscaling plot-level inventory using sub-meter GaoFen satellite data
nodes.venue: Earth System Science Data
nodes.abstract: Southwest China has emerged as a key global carbon stock due to widespread forest expansion and aboveground biomass (AGB) increases driven by major ecological restoration since 2000, making accurate AGB estimates vital for assessing restoration efficacy. However, existing global and national-scale AGB products exhibit substantial limitations in this region, with little correlation with National Forest Inventory (NFI) plot and UAV LiDAR data, which is likely related to the pronounced spatial heterogeneity induced by karst landscapes and large-scale restoration efforts that exacerbate mixed-pixel effects. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Canopy Structure-driven Multi-feature Fusion Network (CSMF-Net) designed for high-precision AGB estimation in complex regions. The method takes NFI plot data as ground truth and integrates GaoFen imagery, horizontal structure derived from tree crown segmentation and vertical structure represented by canopy height data. Based on this approach, we generated a fine-grained 30 m AGB dataset (FineKarstAGB) for 2024, covering four provinces in Southwest China (Yunnan, Guizhou, Guangxi, and Hunan). Accuracy assessment against independent NFI plot data demonstrated the model's robust performance ( R 2 =0.69, RMSE = 28.51 Mg ha −1 ), showing no evidence of saturation in high-biomass regions. Furthermore, a structural consistency assessment using an independent UAV LiDAR-derived canopy height model confirmed that FineKarstAGB maintains a strong relationship with forest vertical structure ( R 2 =0.54). Other public datasets showed weak relationships with both NFI observations ( R 2 ≤0.12) and UAV LiDAR-derived canopy height ( R 2 <0.1). Due to the tree-level segmentation, our dataset also quantifies AGB contributions from sparse trees outside forests, thus enabling more comprehensive and spatially explicit carbon accounting. This dataset provides critical support for regional carbon cycle assessments, fine-scale evaluations of ecological restoration outcomes, and progress toward national carbon neutrality targets. The dataset is available at https://doi.org/10.57760/sciencedb.33452 (Li et al., 2026).

nodes.name: Feature-based intelligent recognition algorithm for primary electrical components in power grid primary equipment
nodes.venue: International Conference on Laser, Materials, and Advanced Manufacturing (LMAM 2026)
nodes.abstract: Rough identification of component appearance or basic attributes results in low accuracy for recognizing primary electrical main wiring components in power grids. To address this, the study investigates an intelligent recognition algorithm for primary electrical main wiring components based on feature extraction. It analyzes electrical main wiring diagrams to extract basic graphical elements, merges them according to rules to generate composite shapes, and then constructs more complex composite components based on shape features and spatial combinations, thereby building primary electrical main wiring composite components for power grids. Busbars are characterized using a combination of geometric and topological analysis, while other components are characterized using shape-based and connection-based methods to extract features of primary equipment electrical main wiring components. Multi-dimensional features are fused and validated with topological relationships. A random forest classifier outputs component type labels, and recalculated feature vectors for non-compliant components adjust the classification, achieving intelligent recognition of primary equipment electrical main wiring components. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves over 90% accuracy in identifying primary equipment components in the electrical main wiring of power grids. Even under high noise intensity of 55 dB, its confidence level remains at 0.97, significantly higher than the 0.61–0.85 range of the comparison methods. Furthermore, the confusion matrix exhibits higher values along the main diagonal and fewer misclassifications, effectively enhancing the accuracy of component identification.

nodes.name: International Conference on Laser, Materials, and Advanced Manufacturing (LMAM 2026)
EKSPLORASI INTEGRASI INQUIRY DAN PROJECT-BASED LEARNING SEBAGAI DASAR PENGEMBANGAN MODEL IMED UNTUK LITERASI MULTIMODAL SISWA SMP
nodes.venue: EDUCATOR : Jurnal Inovasi Tenaga Pendidik dan Kependidikan
nodes.abstract: ABSTRACT The development of digital information requires students not only to produce multimodal content but also to explore, evaluate, and process information critically. This study aims to identify multimodal literacy learning needs, explore existing inquiry and Project-Based Learning (PjBL) practices, and formulate the preliminary characteristics of the Digital Ethnopedagogical Multimodal Inquiry (IMED) model. An exploratory qualitative approach employing a multisite case study design was conducted at three junior high schools in Langsa, Indonesia. Data were collected through classroom observations, semi-structured interviews with six Indonesian language teachers and 12 students, and an analysis of instructional documents and student products. Thematic analysis was conducted by examining data within each case and comparing findings across cases. The results indicate that students have produced various multimodal products and used digital technology in learning. However, inquiry practices tend to focus on information retrieval, while information evaluation and processing remain inconsistent; PjBL is more prominently oriented toward product creation. The integration of these approaches has not yet established a coherent learning sequence. Local wisdom has also not been systematically incorporated as a source of inquiry. These findings provide a basis for formulating the preliminary IMED model, which connects information exploration and evaluation, multimodal production, communication, and reflection, supported by digital technology and local cultural contexts. The model requires further validation and empirical testing. ABSTRAK Perkembangan informasi digital menuntut siswa tidak hanya mampu menghasilkan konten multimodal, tetapi juga mengeksplorasi, mengevaluasi, dan mengolah informasi secara kritis. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi kebutuhan pembelajaran literasi multimodal, mengeksplorasi praktik inquiry dan Project-Based Learning (PjBL), serta merumuskan karakteristik awal model Inquiry Multimodal Etnopedagogis Digital (IMED). Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif eksploratif dengan desain studi kasus multisitus pada tiga sekolah menengah pertama di Kota Langsa, Indonesia. Data dikumpulkan melalui observasi pembelajaran, wawancara semi-terstruktur dengan enam guru Bahasa Indonesia dan 12 siswa, serta analisis dokumen pembelajaran dan produk siswa. Analisis tematik dilakukan melalui pemeriksaan data dalam setiap kasus dan perbandingan antarkasus. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa siswa telah menghasilkan beragam produk multimodal dan menggunakan teknologi digital dalam pembelajaran. Namun, praktik inquiry masih cenderung berfokus pada pencarian informasi, sedangkan evaluasi dan pengolahannya belum konsisten; PjBL lebih menonjol pada proses pembuatan produk. Integrasi keduanya belum membentuk alur pembelajaran yang berkesinambungan. Kearifan lokal juga belum dimanfaatkan secara sistematis sebagai sumber penyelidikan. Temuan ini menjadi dasar perumusan awal IMED yang menghubungkan eksplorasi dan evaluasi informasi, produksi multimodal, komunikasi, serta refleksi dengan dukungan teknologi digital dan konteks budaya lokal. Model tersebut masih memerlukan validasi dan pengujian empiris lebih lanjut.

Cross-Level Gated Dual-Attention Network for Landslide Segmentation in Remote Sensing Imagery
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate landslide segmentation from remote sensing imagery is essential for rapid disaster assessment and geohazard monitoring. However, complex background interference, large variations in landslide scale, irregular boundaries, and the semantic gap between shallow and deep features remain major challenges for precise segmentation. To address these issues, this study proposes CLGDA-Net, a cross-level gated dual-attention network for landslide segmentation in remote sensing imagery. Firstly, a cross-level gated context fusion module (CLGCFM) is introduced into the skip connections to adaptively integrate adjacent shallow and deep features. Specifically, the deep features are spatially aligned with shallow features and dynamically fused through an adaptive gated feature fusion mechanism, followed by receptive-field enhancement to strengthen multi-scale contextual representation. Secondly, a multi-dilation context attention module (MDCAM) is designed at the bottleneck to capture contextual information under different receptive fields using parallel dilated convolutions and to selectively emphasize informative responses. Furthermore, a multi-scale dual-attention fusion module (MSDAFM) is developed to aggregate multi-level decoder features through dual-pooling scale-aware channel attention and scale-adaptive spatial attention, thereby enhancing complementary information across both scale and spatial dimensions. Extensive experiments on Landslide4Sense and Bijie demonstrate that CLGDA-Net achieves competitive segmentation performance and effectively improves the delineation of landslide regions under complex remote sensing environments. Specifically, CLGDA-Net achieves Dice/MCC/Jaccard scores of 0.7315/0.7187/0.5774 on Landslide4Sense and 0.8316/0.8126/0.7118 on Bijie. Moreover, ablation studies verify the effectiveness of the proposed modules, highlighting the positive contributions of cross-level gated fusion and dual-attention feature enhancement to landslide segmentation. These findings suggest that CLGDA-Net has strong potential for practical applications in rapid landslide mapping, post-disaster assessment, and geohazard monitoring based on remote sensing imagery.

nodes.name: CBAM-enhanced MaxViT-Tiny for gastrointestinal endoscopy image classification: Robustness, explainability, and external validation
nodes.abstract: Automated classification of the huge number of images generated during gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is required for reliable and interpretable diagnosis, but there is concern about the vulnerability of deep models to adversarial perturbations. In the current study, a MaxViT-Tiny backbone with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) head is used for 8-class classification of the Kvasir endoscopic images. After deleting duplicate images, 3,996 images remained, which were split into a training set (70%), a validation set (15%) and a test set (15%); the model was compared with five backbones using the same CBAM head under three random seeds. The proposed model obtained the highest test accuracy of 94.33%, a macro F1 score of 0.9431, and a macro area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.9975, with a mean accuracy of 93.72 ± 1.06% across all seeds. White-box FGSM, PGD, CW-L2, and MI-FGSM attacks greatly reduced the accuracy: after adversarial fine-tuning, the accuracy under FGSM was 74.17%, while the accuracy under PGD and MI-FGSM was below 4%, showing poor cross-attack generalization. A preliminary attack detector obtained an AUC of 0.857. Grad-CAM++, Score-CAM, and GradientSHAP sometimes identified clinically relevant regions, but also sometimes focused on non-anatomical artefacts. High accuracy on clean images, even with attention augmentation, therefore does not imply high accuracy on adversarial images or reliable explanations, and the model needs further verification on independent datasets and multi-centre validation before clinical use.

nodes.name: Background-Robust Static Hand Gesture Recognition with Synthetic Scene Compositing: A Grouped Fivefold Ablation Across Five CNN Backbones
nodes.abstract: Abstract Static hand gesture recognition models typically achieve high performance on small RGB datasets but exhibit reduced robustness as background complexity increases. This study investigates whether synthetic scene compositing can mitigate this vulnerability by employing a leakage-aware evaluation protocol. The proposed pipeline integrates alpha-matting-based foreground extraction with random scene compositing and is evaluated using a fivefold protocol that groups images at the image level, ensuring that augmented siblings from the same source image remain within the same fold. Five ImageNet-pretrained convolutional neural network (CNN) backbones are evaluated: EfficientNetV2B0, ResNet50, MobileNetV3Small, DenseNet121, and VGG16. Across 73 configurations and 363-fold runs from a single random seed, the complete pipeline increases mean validation accuracy from 48.0% in the four-class no-synthesis baseline to 97.1%. All 43 synthetic-baseline paired contrasts remain significant after Benjamini and Hochberg correction (q < 0.05, paired t test). The pairedWilcoxon test is constrained by the fivefold minimum attainable two-sided p-value of ≈ 0.0625. The protocol preserves transfer gap visibility: on a reservedHaGRID slice, direct transfer accuracy ranges from 66.2% to 87.7% across 67 synthetic augmented configurations, representing a mean decrease of 17.6 percentage points relative to internal validation (NO SYNTH excluded). An auxiliary MediaPipe Hands plus support vector machine (SVM) baseline achieves 59.2% accuracy and 58.0% macro F1, primarily because landmark detection is successful on only 37.3% of that external slice. Progressive unfreezing underperforms standard fine-tuning in all paired comparisons (18/18 pairs favor standard fine-tuning; 13/18 remain significant after BH FDR correction). Attention and spatial pooling heads do not outperform a plain global average pooling head. Code, raw per-fold JSON outputs, and reproduction scripts are available athttps://github.com/RageLog/bg-robust-rps.

nodes.name: AI-assisted adaptive-optical robotic metrology for sub-millimeter localization and dimensional measurement of blind holes
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Introduction The process of measuring the dimensions of a blind hole is difficult because the interior surfaces and base are hard to probe using normal probes and camera equipment. Optical measurement is additionally affected by restricted visibility, lighting differences, reflectance, view angle, and robotic positioning accuracy. Methods An adaptive robotic optical metrology system using AI is suggested to achieve non-contact hole inspection in this paper. The system consists of a six DOF robot, an optical measurement head with a camera, adaptive lighting system, AI segmentation, sub-pixel circle and ellipse detection, and robot-camera calibration with error correction using CMM reference data. The system was tested using 30 samples having holes with diameter ranges of 5-15 mm, depth range of 10-45 mm, aspect ratio of 2.0-3.1, three different surface reflectivity conditions, and angle range of 0-20°. Results All trials were successfully carried out for detecting the holes. Average position error in the three-dimensional space was 0.0322 mm; the RMSE of position error was 0.0344 mm; the maximum position error was 0.0645 mm. The average absolute diameter error was 0.0544 mm; RMSE of the absolute diameter error was 0.0647 mm. Average repeatability was 0.0217 mm; average confidence in AI-based segmentation was 0.935. Average position errors varied between 0.026 mm and 0.037 mm depending on reflectivity classes and increased at 15° and higher approach angles. Discussion The results offer initial proof-of-concept validation for the use of AI-aided adaptive optical robotic systems to perform automated and contactless inspections of blind holes at least within the current scope of operation. Nevertheless, the small number of samples used, single replication and partially confounding experimental conditions pose a limit on the generalizability of the results. Additional research is necessary using multiple trials, ablation tests of modules, and larger depth-to-diameter ratios are required to establish the system’s robustness and measurement reliability.
